provenance.paper_title: WorldMM: Dynamic Multimodal Memory Agent for Long Video Reasoning

representation_paths.memory_component: timestamped frames and searchable segment features

evidence.paraphrase: WorldMM stores segment features for text-to-video similarity search and a timestamp-to-frame index for direct visual inspection.

representation_paths.memory_component: multi-scale event graphs and evolving semantic graph

evidence.paraphrase: Episodic knowledge graphs span multiple temporal scales; a semantic graph stores long-term relations, and a retrieval agent iteratively chooses memory type and query.

Matched old and new triplets are sent to an LLM to identify outdated facts and revised or added facts. For WorldMM, this specifically supports LLM-based resolution of conflicting records of timestamped frames and searchable segment features.

Embedding similarity finds overlapping triplets before consolidation integrates new conceptual knowledge. For WorldMM, this specifically supports merging or deduplication of overlapping entries of timestamped frames and searchable segment features.

Semantic triplets and recurring habits are extracted from video segments and consolidated into a reusable long-term semantic graph. For WorldMM, this specifically supports abstraction of episodes into reusable experience of timestamped frames and searchable segment features.

derived.hybrid_relation: Graph-derived time ranges can directly index original frames, while feature search independently retrieves visual segments.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 4): During inference, the operative memory component (timestamped frames and searchable segment features) changes through LLM-based resolution of conflicting records, merging or deduplication of overlapping entries, abstraction of episodes into reusable experience; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
